content: 1. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of fezolinetant by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors increases fezolinetant's AUC and peak plasma concentration. 2. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration of flibanserin with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 3. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Alosetron is associated with serious, potentially life-threatening, dose-related gastrointestinal adverse effects, and co-administration with CYP1A2 inhibitors should generally be avoided. 4. Aluminum hydroxide decreases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug, or separate administration by at least 2 hours. 5. Aminolevulinic acid (oral) and ciprofloxacin may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid administering other phototoxic drugs with aminolevulinic acid oral for 24 hours during the perioperative period. 6. Ciprofloxacin increases the toxicity of aminolevulinic acid (topical) through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of photosensitizing drugs may enhance phototoxic reactions during photodynamic therapy with aminolevulinic acid. 7. Amisulpride and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administered. 8. Anagrelide and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Ciprofloxacin decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Antibiotics may diminish the therapeutic effects of BCG. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 10. Buprenorphine (all forms) and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Carbonyl iron decreases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Administer ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after carbonyl iron. 12. Ceritinib and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Ciprofloxacin decreases the efficacy of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of the cholera vaccine with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may act against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 14. Clarithromycin and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Concurrent use of drugs that prolong the QT interval may result in additive effects and increased risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Therapy should be carefully monitored. 16. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of clozapine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Use caution when administering ciprofloxacin in patients receiving drugs that prolong the QT interval. Clozapine and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. 17. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If short-term (14 days or less) use of moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the cobimetinib dose to 20 mg. Resume the full dose after discontinuation of the CYP3A inhibitor. 18. Desflurane and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Didanosine decreases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after didanosine. 20. Dofetilide increases ciprofloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Ciprofloxacin and dronedarone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. The use of dronedarone with other QT-prolonging medications is contraindicated. 22. Eliglustat and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Encorafenib and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Ciprofloxacin and entrectinib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Eribulin and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Fexinidazole and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of fexinidazole with drugs known to block potassium channels or prolong the QT interval. 27. Ciprofloxacin and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs during initiation, concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or changes from baseline by more than 60 ms. 28. Ciprofloxacin and glasdegib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of QTc interval prolongation. 29. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Ciprofloxacin increases ibrutinib levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term, interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 31. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Concurrent use of QT-prolonging drugs may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Therapy should be carefully monitored. 32. Inotuzumab and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs and electrolytes before and after initiation, and monitor periodically during treatment. 33. Iron sucrose decreases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Administer ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after iron sucrose. 34. Isoflurane and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Ivosidenib and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of QTc interval prolongation. 36. Lasmiditan increases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Lefamulin and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with weak CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, adjust the lonafarnib dose accordingly and monitor for arrhythmias. 39. Macimorelin and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 40. Mefloquine increases ciprofloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Ciprofloxacin and methyl aminolevulinate may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Ciprofloxacin decreases the effects of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota. 43. Mirtazapine and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Olanzapine and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose. 46. Ciprofloxacin and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. ECG monitoring is recommended in high-risk patients. 47. Oxaliplatin and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Ciprofloxacin and panobinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of pirfenidone by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Ciprofloxacin and pitolisant both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Ciprofloxacin increases pomalidomide levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 52. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of rasagiline by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor patients closely for adverse reactions. 53. Ribociclib increases ciprofloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 54. Selinexor and ciprofloxacin have an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 55. Sevoflurane and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 56. Siponimod and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 57. Sotorasib decreases ciprofloxacin levels by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 58. Tepotinib increases ciprofloxacin levels by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 59. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of theophylline by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor theophylline levels and adjust dosage as needed. 60. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of tizanidine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 61. Ciprofloxacin and toremifene both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 62. Ciprofloxacin and tretinoin both increase the risk of phototoxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 63. Trilaciclib decreases ciprofloxacin levels through OCT2, MATE1, and MATE-2K inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
